questions.q: The lab starts with $[2, 3, 3, 4, 6, 8, 14, 18, 18, 18, 19]$. What are the mean, median and mode?
questions.explain: Sum $= 113$, so mean $= 113/11 \approx 10.27$. The 6th of 11 sorted values is $8$ (median). $18$ appears three times, more than any other value (mode).

questions.q: You drag the rightmost point from $19$ to $30$. What happens?
options: Mean and median both rise by 1
The median rises; the mean stays the same
Nothing changes because the mode is still 18
The mean rises to $\approx 11.27$; the median stays at $8$
questions.explain: The sum grows by $11$, so the mean grows by $11/11 = 1$. The middle value is still $8$: the median is robust to outliers, the mean chases them.

questions.q: You add a 12th point at $20$ (even count). What is the new median?
questions.explain: With 12 sorted values the median is the average of the 6th and 7th: $(8 + 14)/2 = 11$. $\approx 11.08$ is the new mean, not the median.

questions.q: Reporting the "typical" house price in a town where one billionaire's mansion is far above all other prices, which measure best resists that outlier?
questions.explain: The median depends only on the middle of the sorted values, so one extreme value barely moves it, while the mean is pulled toward the outlier.
